title: Calibrating Reproduced Claims in Recommender Systems
abstract: arXiv:2609.26975v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reproduction studies can produce mixed outcomes. Reported values may differ while the ordering of the compared methods remains the same, a result may hold only under some experimental conditions, or a released implementation may fail to reproduce a result that the model can still reach. The terms repeatability, reproducibility, and replicability describe how a follow-up study relates to the original experiment, but not which parts of the original claim are supported by the new results. We introduce \emph{claim calibration} as a way of stating the strongest claim supported by a follow-up study, together with the conditions under which it holds and the parts that remain untested. We apply this perspective to five original--follow-up paper pairs from recommender-systems research. translated_title: 校准推荐系统中的复现结论
translated_abstract: 复现研究可能产生混杂的结果：报告的数值可能不同，但被比较方法的排序保持不变；某一结果可能仅在部分实验条件下成立；或者已发布的实现无法复现模型本身仍能达到的结果。“可重复性”“可复现性”“可再现性”这些术语描述的是后续研究与原始实验之间的关系，但并未说明原始结论中有哪些部分得到了新结果的支持。我们提出“结论校准”这一概念，用以表述后续研究所能支持的最强结论，同时说明该结论成立的条件以及尚未被验证的部分。我们将这一视角应用于推荐系统研究中的五对原始论文与后续论文。这些案例表明，数值上的吻合、方法排序、统计结果以及整体结论之间并不总是一致的，而且后续研究……（原文截断）
tldr: 本文提出“结论校准”这一新概念，用于精确陈述复现研究所支持的最强结论及其成立条件，并通过对推荐系统领域五对原作—复现论文的分析，揭示了数值一致、方法排序、统计结果与整体结论之间的错位。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "claim calibration," a framework for stating the strongest claim supported by a reproduction study along with the conditions under which it holds, and shows through five original–followup paper pairs in recommender systems research that agreement in numerical values, method rankings, statistical results, and overall conclusions does not always coincide.
